title: Constant words are computable in linear time
statement: For every fixed Boolean word $w$, there are a finite Turing machine $M$ over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean input $x$, $M$ outputs $w$ and halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps.
replaced:
For every fixed Boolean word $w$ there exist a multi-tape Turing machine $M$
over the Boolean alphabet and a constant $c$ such that $M$ computes the
constant function $x \mapsto w$ in time $c \cdot (n + 1)$: on every input $x$,
within $c \cdot (\abs{x} + 1)$ steps $M$ halts with output exactly $w$.
